text:
jordan: Heads up team — launching a "Burst Protection Buffer" next Thursday to reduce surprise overage spikes for customers on the free tier and PAYG. It smooths very short token bursts by queuing/slicing requests for up to 20s. Details: https://redwood.internal/policies/burst-protection

kevin: Quick Q: does this change invoicing or free credits consumption?

jordan: No change to how tokens are invoiced. Free credits are consumed only for completed token output. The buffer delays token generation rather than charging for held requests. Finance will post a short note for customers about visibility on invoices.

tess: Will users see errors or retries? Any headers we return so SDKs can detect buffering?

jordan: We'll add X-Redwood-Buffer: active and a Buffer-Delay header with ms. Typical delay <20s; SDKs should backoff and respect the header. We won't return 429s for buffered requests unless the buffer fills.

finance-bot: For audit: if buffering causes a timeout/failed completion on our side, we will auto-issue a one-off credit upon investigation.

support: Adding KB entry and canned replies. ETA: tomorrow morning.

kevin: Rollout plan?

jordan: Staged canary Friday 10:00 PT -> 25% -> 100% over 24h. Monitor buffer_fill_rate, failed_completions, p95 latency. Abort criteria: >3% increase in failed completions.

kevin: Sounds good. We'll coordinate customer comms.

jordan: TL;DR: Burst Protection Buffer to smooth short spikes, no invoice model change, headers for detection, staged rollout. :)
